item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 102317
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located well northwest of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Storm Norbert, located several hundred miles west-
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms located more than 500 miles
to the southeast of the Hawaiian Islands are associated with a broad
trough of low pressure. Some gradual development of this system is
possible over the next few days into the weekend while it moves
generally northward and then meanders to the southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

Central and Western East Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure are located several hundred miles southwest of the
southwestern coast of Mexico. Gradual development of this system is
anticipated, and a tropical depression is likely to form by early
next week while it moves generally west-northwestward to westward
over the central and western portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...NORBERT GRADUALLY INTENSIFYING OVER OPEN WATERS... As of 5:00 PM HST Thu Sep 10 the center of Norbert was located near 16.4, -121.9 with movement W at 14 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1000 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 110238
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026
 
...NORBERT GRADUALLY INTENSIFYING OVER OPEN WATERS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.4N 121.9W
ABOUT 900 MI...1450 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 16.4 North, longitude 121.9 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h), and this general 
motion is expected to continue through Friday, with a turn to the 
west-northwest likely on Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Some strengthening is forecast, and Norbert could 
become a hurricane this weekend.  
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026 
406 
WTPZ44 KNHC 110239
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026

Norbert continues to show a shear pattern on satellite imagery, 
with the center located on the western edge of a strong and growing 
area of convection.  Objective satellite estimates are higher than 
the last advisory, so the initial intensity is nudged upward to 45 
kt.  Only slow strengthening is anticipated for the next few 
days while Norbert experiences light-to-moderate westerly shear 
over warm waters, though close to some dry mid-level air.  Thus, 
Norbert will likely have some challenges developing an inner core, 
probably preventing any rapid changes in the near-term.  Model 
guidance is higher than the last cycle overall, and the new 
intensity forecast is raised slightly from the previous one.  The 
long-range intensity is a challenge given the large latitudinal 
spread in the track guidance as well as the possibility of 
increasing shear.  

The tropical storm's motion remains westward at 12 kt.  A mid- 
level ridge over the eastern Pacific is forecast to build westward 
in tandem with Norbert during the next few days, keeping the 
cyclone moving westward to west-northwestward.  A south-of-west 
track is possible by next week, depending on the future orientation 
of the ridge and the position of Norbert.  The ECMWF has been 
showing this west-southwest motion for a few runs now, and with the 
Google DeepMind now in closer agreement, the official forecast is 
shifted southward at long range.  Otherwise few changes were made 
to the previous forecast.
